title: Reproducibility package for controlled multi-regime evaluation of drug-target affinity models
description:
Reproducibility materials for Model Rankings in Drug–Target Affinity Prediction Vary Across Evaluation Regimes: A Controlled Multi-Seed Study of Model-Comparison Reliability.

Version v1.1.2 corrects the public export of Supplementary Table S11 Part 2. The corrected export contains 12 seedwise Kendall rank-correlation rows for two replacement model sets: mean-pooling and max_len=1000. In each replacement set, only ConcatFusion is replaced; the other four models remain unchanged. This is a correction to the existing reproducibility distribution and does not represent additional experiments, new model training, or independent experimental replication.

The evidence comprises 282 runs: 126 original KIBA/Davis runs, 36 AdamW capacity-control runs, 30 runs on a second KIBA cold-start split, and 90 within-cohort runs on human GPCR Ki (30) and protease Ki (60). Historical 36-run Adam exploration is auxiliary and excluded from the formal evidence total.

S11 Part 2 calculation protocol: Model rankings are based on record-level C-index. Each seed is evaluated separately. Five models produce ten pairwise model comparisons. Kendall tau follows the original convention, tau = (C - D) / 10, where C and D denote the numbers of concordant and discordant model pairs, respectively. The seed order is 42, 123, and 2026. The previous six-row export contained seedwise correlations for the original five-model set rather than the required two replacement model sets.

These CSVs are document-table transcriptions; their inclusion does not imply independent recomputation from raw record-level predictions.

The package includes training, preparation and evaluation code; configurations; frozen partition membership and checksums; run-level and aggregate metrics; prediction-only projections; histories; statistical summaries; and corrected table exports. The 69 independently checksummed ZIP parts are retained under revisions/v1.1.0/payload_parts/ and are extracted with the included unpacking tool. Third-party source structures, protein sequences and affinity labels are not redistributed. Model weights and large execution logs are omitted from this lightweight distribution; the omission inventory is explicit. Complete original-126 artifacts and original bootstrap random-number-generator states were not retained.

The GPCR/protease extension contains two non-kinase target classes. GPCR cold-target includes seven independent test sequences. Protease splits share two test sequences and 163 cold-drug entities and are split-sensitivity evaluations of one cohort, not two independently collected external cohorts. External model capacities are unequal. These results do not establish universal rank reversal, causal fusion superiority, prospective discovery or zero-shot cross-family transfer.

Final statistical corrections: S17 errors are raw-scale; S13 Delta = C-index(A) - C-index(B); S18 reports paired mean and sample standard deviation rather than bootstrap intervals; S22 sample standard deviation uses ddof=1. Historical numerical artifacts retain their provenance; final table descriptions govern the corrected presentation.
